🚀 Cybertruck 2 Year Review: Is It Still Worth It in 2026?
 📷Two years after taking delivery, here’s my honest, no-filter look at living with the Tesla Cybertruck every single day.

If you’re thinking about buying a Cybertruck in 2026, or you already own one and want to hear real long-term thoughts, this review is for you.

NEURALINK IS ABOUT TO RESTORE SIGHT TO THE BLIND AND HEARING TO THE DEAF

Neuralink’s long-term vision goes far beyond helping paralyzed people control computers with their thoughts.

The next frontier is restoring lost senses:
•  Blindsight — A Neuralink implant that can restore vision even for people who are completely blind. It starts at low resolution and improves over time as the system learns.
•  Hearing restoration — Similar brain-interface technology is being developed to bypass damaged ears and directly stimulate the auditory cortex, potentially bringing hearing back to the deaf.
Elon Musk has been clear about the ambition:
“Blindsight will enable those who have even complete loss of vision to see in low resolution at first, leading to high resolution over time.”
This is not science fiction anymore.
It’s the beginning of reversing disabilities that have been considered permanent for centuries.
Neuralink is turning the page from “managing disability” to “restoring full human capability.”
The impact could be life-changing for millions.

NEURALINK IS ALREADY CHANGING LIVES — AND IT’S JUST GETTING STARTED

Neuralink isn’t a distant sci-fi concept anymore.

It’s real, it’s implanted in humans right now, and it’s restoring capabilities that were once considered permanently lost.

Here’s why Neuralink’s impact is so profound:
•  Restoring independence to paralyzed people — Patients who lost use of their hands or entire bodies can now move cursors, type, play games, and browse the internet using only their thoughts. No joysticks, no eye-tracking, no assistants needed.
•  Blindsight on the horizon — The next major leap (pending approval) is restoring vision even for people who are completely blind, starting at low resolution and improving over time.
•  Full body functionality coming — The long-term goal is to give people with spinal cord injuries or neurological damage full control of their limbs again — walking, using hands, regaining independence.
•  Human-AI symbiosis — Beyond fixing disabilities, Neuralink is building a high-bandwidth link between the brain and AI so humanity can keep pace with superintelligence instead of being left behind.
Elon Musk on Neuralink’s mission:
“The goal of Neuralink is to achieve a symbiosis with AI, to help humans keep up with AI and not be left behind.”
This is more than medical technology.
This is the beginning of the next chapter of human evolution — where disabilities are reversed, dignity is restored, and humanity gains the tools to thrive alongside superintelligent AI.
Neuralink is moving faster than almost any medical technology in history — and the best is still ahead.

ELON MUSK ON THE TRUE COST OF SHORT-TERM THINKING

Most leaders optimize for the next quarter or the next election cycle.

Elon Musk thinks in decades and centuries.
He has repeatedly warned that short-term thinking is one of the biggest threats to civilization:

“The biggest mistake people make is they think in the short term instead of the long term. The long term is what matters.”
This philosophy explains almost everything he does:
•  SpaceX is building Starship for Mars, not just low-Earth orbit tourism
•  Tesla is pushing sustainable energy for the next 100 years, not just the next earnings report
•  xAI is building truth-seeking AI to understand the universe, not to chase quarterly ad revenue
•  Neuralink is working on long-term human-AI symbiosis so we don’t get left behind by superintelligence
Elon’s willingness to endure years of ridicule, near-bankruptcy, and relentless criticism comes from this long-term view. He’s playing a different game — one where the scoreboard is measured in human progress across generations, not stock price movements.
Short-term thinking gives you quick wins and applause.
Long-term thinking gives you reusable rockets, affordable EVs, and a path to becoming multiplanetary.
The future belongs to those who can delay gratification and think in centuries.

🚨 Big win for free speech: The US Justice Department just told France “No” on helping their investigation into Elon Musk’s 𝕏.
After raiding 𝕏’s Paris office and summoning Musk over “algorithm bias,” deepfakes, CSAM, and Holocaust denial, France wanted US help enforcing their strict speech laws globally.
DOJ’s letter called it out: This is misusing the justice system to target a US company and undermine the First Amendment.
Why this is good:
•  Protects American platforms from foreign governments dictating what speech is allowed online.
•  Rejects exporting Europe’s heavy-handed content rules (where questioning history or “biased” algorithms can be crimes) to the US.
•  Stands up for open discourse over “digital sovereignty” theater.
•  Actual crimes like real CSAM deserve proper channels—not fishing expeditions against reduced censorship.
US shouldn’t help allies chill speech on American soil. Free speech isn’t negotiable. 🇺🇸

🚁 Epic drone flyover of Tesla's Fremont Factory!

Captured some incredible and historic footage today:  Cybercabs actively testing — smoothly handling speed bumps before launching hard down the track. I also spotted Model S and Model X vehicles in the launch area along with what appear to be some of the final S & X rolling off the assembly line as their legendary run at Fremont wraps up.

The Model Y production line was surprisingly quiet during the flight, but I got great aerial views of the busy shipping yard and the factory’s recycling area too.

From next-gen Cybercab action to the end of an era with the S & X — this flyover really shows the transition happening at one of the world’s most important EV factories. Fremont never disappoints!

What do you think about the Cybercab testing and the final S/X coming off the line? Drop your thoughts in the comments 👇
